chunks: 2053 - Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
To one of his followers on the Day of al-Fiṭr, while he was supplicating for him: “O so-and-so, may Allah accept from you and from us.”
He said: Then he remained until it was the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and he said to him: “O so-and-so, may Allah accept from us and from you.”
He said: So I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, you said one thing on al-Fiṭr, and you say on al-Aḍḥā something different from it.”

So he said: “Yes. I said to him on al-Fiṭr, ‘May Allah accept from you and from us,’ because he did the like of my act, and he and I were equal in the act. And I said to him on al-Aḍḥā, ‘May Allah accept from us and from you,’ because we are able to offer sacrifice, while he is not able to offer sacrifice; so we did other than his act.”

key_terms.الْفِعْلِ: the act or deed being performed
key_terms.تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ: may Allah accept; a formula asking divine acceptance of deeds
key_terms.يَدْعُو: he supplicates; making du'a for someone
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفِطْرِ: the day of Eid al-Fiṭr, marking the end of sawm
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْأَضْحَىٰ: the day of Eid al-Aḍḥā, associated with sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say “May Allah accept from you and from us” on Eid al-Fiṭr but “from us and from you” on Eid al-Aḍḥā?
ai.summary: This hadith reports how al-Riḍā عليه السلام varied the wording of his du'a on Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā according to the deeds actually performed. On Eid al-Fiṭr, he placed the other person first because their acts were equal, while on Eid al-Aḍḥā he placed "us" first because the Imam and his household could perform the sacrifice and the other person could not. The narration highlights precision in supplication and attentiveness to the realities of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2053 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudhayl, from Al-Ridha (as), who said:

"Imam (as) said to one of his companions on the Day of Eid al-Fitr while supplicating for him:
'O so-and-so, may Allah (swt) accept (the deeds) from you and from us.'

Then, on the Day of Eid al-Adha, Imam (as) said to him:
'O so-and-so, may Allah (swt) accept (the deeds) from us and from you.'
I asked Imam (as): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), on Eid al-Fitr you said something, and on Eid al-Adha you said something different. Why?'

Imam (as) replied: 'Yes, I said to him on Eid al-Fitr, "May Allah (swt) accept (the deeds) from you and from us," because he did the same as I did, and our actions were the same. But on Eid al-Adha, I said to him, "May Allah (swt) accept (the deeds) from us and from you," because we are able to offer a sacrifice, whereas he is not able to do so. Thus, our actions differed.'"
